Run an interactive construction estimating workflow using the connected PlanSwift and Microsoft Excel (Desktop) tools on the SAME Windows workstation. This saved task uses the executable desktop connector added in AURA PR #693; it replaces the export-only approach of the earlier proposed pilot. It has not been run on Daniel's computer.

Before execution, obtain the exact open PlanSwift job name, drawing revision, quantity scope (measurements OR parts), approved rate-book filename, rate effective date, currency, material waste percentage, markup percentage, tax percentage and tax basis (materials OR subtotal_with_markup). Obtain explicit confirmation that the measurements and scope have been reviewed. Ask for missing inputs; do not invent defaults, prices, measurements or confirmations. Both applications must be connected and verified on the same workstation. If absent, direct the user to connect PlanSwift and Microsoft Excel (Desktop) using the downloadable Windows connector. Keep the workstation online.

Execute these supported operations in sequence:
1. planswift.job.read on PlanSwift with the exact job_name, revision and quantity_scope. This captures existing takeoff items directly; it does not measure new drawings. Retain the returned takeoff snapshot_id and row_count.
2. excel.ratebooks.list on Microsoft Excel (Desktop). Select the user-approved workbook from the returned filenames.
3. excel.rates.read with that rate_book and explicit as_of date. Retain its returned rates snapshot_id. Missing, expired or overlapping rates and mismatched cost codes/units must block pricing.
4. After the user reviews the quantities and costing parameters, excel.estimate.create using the exact snapshot IDs returned above plus the supplied currency, material_waste_percent, markup_percent, tax_percent, tax_basis and measurements_reviewed=true only if the user explicitly confirmed review. Respect AURA's approval step. The connector applies deterministic formulas, recalculates with actual installed Excel and checks the saved values. Never manufacture a workbook receipt or claim success from planned formulas.
5. excel.estimate.get using the returned report_id. Verify the saved report matches its creation receipt. Present AURA's downloadable Excel estimate and a concise summary of job/revision, row count, rate date, currency, total and costing assumptions. The workbook remains a draft pending final acceptance.

Do not combine measurement and part scopes, sum unlike units, guess conversions, replace missing rates with zero, or modify the PlanSwift job or source rate book. Repeat identical inputs by reconciling/reusing the existing report. If the workstation is offline, inputs change, Excel is locked, or a formula/file check fails, show the actual blocker and preserve prior work. No email or Discord messages. This first release uses the standard Summary/Takeoff/Rates/Estimate workbook layout; a separate mapping is needed for an arbitrary existing Excel template. Validate a known completed job on the real workstation before production reliance or unattended certification.
